issue.title: Attribute schema save latency by stage before choosing bob albums/bank config update trims
issue.description:
Proposed by bob-cli-mf.10 (notes #1, #2, #7), triaged by the bob-cli-mf land agent.
Evidence: file:explicit:320a6276021490979e5d934b (bob-cli-mf.10-acceptance.tar.gz).

Epic bob-cli-mf made every schema arrangement one guarded transaction. Its plan proposed
bob-cli save-latency trims: embed the post-write album entry or bank config report in the
update JSON to drop the blocking `bob albums list` (~0.65 s estimate), scope
`verify_installed` to the edited album, and let bob declare quietness (`index_changed`).
The measured end-to-end numbers do not attribute time to those stages:

- Final real-Obsidian saves: album 458.1 ms, bank 523.6 ms (one sample each).
- Album applyMs 513.9 ms; settled dry-run p50/p95 525.5/529 ms (n=6).
- Bank config apply p50/p95 157.5/178 ms; revalidation 17.5/18 ms (n=2).
- The album report does not isolate the post-apply `bob albums list` duration, so the
  ~650 ms estimate is unverified.

Proposal: add per-stage timings (pre-sync, plan, commit, verify, post-sync, report
refresh) to `bob albums update` / `bob bank config update` JSON or debug output, and/or
to the plugin's albumSchemaTimings / bankSetupTimings spans. Collect repeatable save
samples, then pick only the trims the attribution supports. Treat `--offline`
interactive saves as a separate product decision.

task_type_fields.proposal: Add per-stage timings to bob albums update and bob bank config update saves (and the plugin timing spans), collect repeatable samples, then choose among embedding the post-write report, scoping verify_installed, and an index_changed quietness flag.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic bob-cli-mf forbade bob-cli changes and its acceptance measurements could not attribute latency to specific CLI stages.

issue.creation_reason: bob-cli-mf.10 measured album and bank schema saves end to end but could not attribute time to the post-write albums list or verify stages, so the plan's proposed CLI latency trims are unsupported until measured.
